live.name: softmax_belief_listener
live.hypothesis: Listeners evaluate candidate referents through pragmatic counterfactual reasoning, but rather than strictly matching choice probabilities to posterior beliefs, they select their click via a bounded-precision softmax decision rule over beliefs. When choosing among semantically valid referents, response sensitivity determines how strongly differences in subjective belief translate into click probabilities, softening extreme pragmatic inferences and generating bounded, probabilistic choice. On uninformative trials, choices likewise reflect this bounded softmax response rule applied over prior perceptual and contextual expectations.

Refining rsa_l1_singleton_feat_color_familiar by incorporating the stochastic transmission noise component from noisy_channel_speaker_l2: listeners perform first-order pragmatic inversion of a speaker who balances literal informativeness against a rich perceptual and experiential referent prior, but occasionally articulates any applicable descriptor by mistake. live.name: bounded_capacity_listener

Rather than executing unconstrained Bayesian belief revision that overwhelmingly eliminates complex competitor objects, a resource-limited listener dampens extreme likelihood ratios to maintain moderate expectations for multi-featured competitors. On uninformative trials where no communicative evidence is received, choices directly reflect prior perceptual and contextual scene expectations.

live.name: pragmatic_preemption_listener
live.hypothesis: Listeners interpret utterances through pragmatic preemption: they recognize that speakers prioritize unambiguous descriptors that uniquely pick out an intended referent, so the presence of an unambiguous distinguishing feature preempts the speaker from using an ambiguous shared descriptor. When hearing a shared descriptor, listeners infer that the speaker intended a referent lacking a unique distinguishing label rather than a competitor for which a uniquely identifying descriptor was available. Across displays with redundant features and large feature gaps, this preemption mechanism prevents the artificial dilution of pragmatic inferences while maintaining calibrated expectations for candidate referents.

A rational pragmatic listener inverts this reliance-sensitive speaker, recognizing that hearing an ambiguous descriptor strongly points toward the candidate referent that lacks alternative descriptive options. This mechanism disagrees most sharply with contrastive similarity models on displays with large feature gaps between a minimal target and a complex competitor, correctly preventing listeners from over-selecting the complex competitor.
